questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the **bracket** first: (33 + 27) = 60.

Perform **multiplication**: 60 × 2 = 120.

Group positive and negative terms: (94 + 36 + 120) − (58 + 91).

Final calculation: 250 − 149 = 101.

**∴ The correct answer is 101.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 94 + 36 − 58 + (33 + 27) × 2 − 91

To solve this expression, we apply the **BODMAS** rule (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 94 + 36 − 58 + 60 × 2 − 91 (Solving **Bracket**)

⇒ 94 + 36 − 58 + 120 − 91 (Solving **Multiplication**)

⇒ 130 − 58 + 120 − 91 (Performing **Addition** from left)

⇒ 72 + 120 − 91 (Performing **Subtraction** from left)

⇒ 192 − 91

⇒ 101

**∴ The correct answer is 101.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule Hierarchy

Operations must be performed in the sequence: **Brackets** (), **Of**, **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−). Addition and Subtraction have the same priority and are usually solved from **left to right**.

Sign Rules

When multiplying signs: (+) × (+) = (+), (−) × (−) = (+), and (+) × (−) = (−). Always perform calculations within the innermost brackets first if multiple brackets are present.

questions.question: 72 + 89 - (39 ÷ 3) + 26 - 14 + 33 of 1 = ?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Solve the core operations: **(39 ÷ 3) = 13** and **33 of 1 = 33**. Combine positive values: 72 + 89 + 26 + 33 = 220. Combine negative values: −13 − 14 = −27. Final calculation: 220 − 27 = 193. **∴ The correct answer is 193.**

questions.question: 8 men can finish the work in 18 days, working 6 hours per day. How many men are required to finish the same work in 12 days, if each works 8 hours per day?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **MDH** formula for work equality: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂

8 × 18 × 6 = M₂ × 12 × 8

864 = M₂ × 96

M₂ = 864 ÷ 96 = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial workforce (M₁) = **8 men**

Initial days (D₁) = **18 days**

Initial hours (H₁) = **6 hr per day**

Target days (D₂) = **12 days**

Target hours (H₂) = **8 hr per day**

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Men × Days × Hours

Since the **work is the same** in both cases: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e4a3ac47978ca3fbead9c61b45878e60f703d1f0dde44de95747060d65775c6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work in man-hours = 8 × 18 × 6

⇒ 864 = M₂ × 12 × 8

⇒ 864 = M₂ × 96

⇒ M₂ = 864 ÷ 96

⇒ M₂ = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The MDH Rule

For any work involving men, days, and hours, the relation is (M₁×D₁×H₁)/W₁ = (M₂×D₂×H₂)/W₂, where W represents the amount of work.

Inverse Proportion in Time & Work

The number of men is inversely proportional to the number of days and hours. If you double the men, the time required is halved for the same amount of work.

Efficiency Factor

If individuals have different efficiencies (E), the formula expands to M₁×D₁×H₁×E₁ = M₂×D₂×H₂×E₂.

questions.question: (5)/(6) - ((1)/(3) times (2)/(5)) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the multiplication first as per **BODMAS**: 1/3 × 2/5 = 2/15.

Calculate the difference using the **LCM** of 6 and 15, which is 30.

Convert fractions: (25 − 4) / 30 = 21/30.

Simplify by dividing by 3: 7/10.

**∴ The correct answer is 7/10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 5/6 − (1/3 × 2/5)

According to the **order of operations**, we solve the parentheses first.

⇒ 5/6 − (1 × 2 / 3 × 5)

⇒ 5/6 − 2/15

⇒ To subtract, find the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of 6 and 15.

⇒ Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, **30**...

⇒ Multiples of 15: 15, **30**...

⇒ Adjusting the fractions: (5 × 5) / (6 × 5) − (2 × 2) / (15 × 2)

⇒ 25/30 − 4/30

⇒ 21/30

⇒ Simplification: 21 ÷ 3 / 30 ÷ 3 = 7/10

**∴ The correct answer is 7/10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Simplification must always follow the order: **Brackets**, **Orders**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Fraction Multiplication

The product of two fractions is the product of their **numerators** divided by the product of their **denominators** (a/b × c/d = ac/bd).

Fraction Subtraction

Subtracting fractions requires a **common denominator**. If denominators are different, use the **LCM** to make them equivalent before performing the operation.

questions.question: Which of the following lies between 3(1)/(5) & 3(3)/(5)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **mixed fractions** into **decimals** for rapid comparison.

Lower limit: 3(1/5) = 3 + 0.2 = **3.2**

Upper limit: 3(3/5) = 3 + 0.6 = **3.6**

Check 3(2/5): 3 + 0.4 = **3.4** (3.2 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Range lower bound = 3(1)/(5)

Range upper bound = 3(3)/(5)

**Method:**

Identify the **decimal values** of the limits and all options to determine which number falls within the **open interval** (3.2, 3.6).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00cc875b425120dc4f8f81e18b7cc76e29c889c3fa1bf6b4778f721fd8c92d8d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Lower limit = 3 + 1/5 = 3 + 0.2 = **3.2**

⇒ Upper limit = 3 + 3/5 = 3 + 0.6 = **3.6**

⇒ Option 1: 3(7/11) = 3 + 0.636 ≈ **3.636** (Outside range)

⇒ Option 2: 3(2/5) = 3 + 0.4 = **3.4** (Inside range: 3.2 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Comparison of Like Fractions

When the **denominator** is the same, the fraction with the larger **numerator** is greater. For mixed numbers, if the whole part is identical, compare only the fractional parts.

Decimal Conversion Shortcut

Standard unit fractions help speed up calculations: 1/5 = 0.2, 1/10 = 0.1, and 1/11 ≈ 0.0909.

Finding Values Between Fractions

To find a value between two fractions, convert them to a **common denominator** or find the **arithmetic mean**: (a + b) ÷ 2.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **sum** of an **arithmetic series** is calculated as: **Sum = Average × Number of terms**.

**Average** = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2 = (21 + 60) ÷ 2 = **40.5**

**Number of terms (n)** = (Last term − First term) + 1 = (60 − 21) + 1 = **40**

**Sum** = 40.5 × 40 = **1620**

**∴ The correct answer is 1620.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The series is 21 + 22 + 23 + ... + 60.

**Formula Used:** Sum of first **n** natural numbers (Σn) = **[n × (n + 1)] ÷ 2**

⇒ Total Sum = (Sum of first 60 natural numbers) − (Sum of first 20 natural numbers)

⇒ Sum (1 to 60) = (60 × 61) ÷ 2

⇒ Sum (1 to 60) = 30 × 61 = **1830**

⇒ Sum (1 to 20) = (20 × 21) ÷ 2

⇒ Sum (1 to 20) = 10 × 21 = **210**

⇒ Required Sum = 1830 − 210 = **1620**

**∴ The correct answer is 1620.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression (AP) Sum

The sum of an **AP** can also be expressed as Sₙ = (n/2) × [2a + (n − 1)d], where **a** is the first term and **d** is the common difference.

Consecutive Integers

For a series of **consecutive integers**, the common difference **d** is always 1, simplifying the number of terms to (Last − First + 1).

Sum of Squares

The sum of squares of the first **n** natural numbers is given by the formula: [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6.

questions.question: The area of a square is 64 square cm. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Side** of the **square** = √**Area** = √64 = 8 cm.

**Perimeter** of the **square** = 4 × **Side** = 4 × 8 = 32 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 32 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Area** of the **square** = 64 cm².

**Formula Used:** **Area** = (**Side**)²; **Perimeter** = 4 × **Side**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a859ca7ebf654f4a1e88ad395fe38e530b2bb16e40dd59daead6f7039d9622d4.png] 

⇒ **Area** = (**Side**)² = 64

⇒ **Side** = √64

⇒ **Side** = 8 cm

⇒ **Perimeter** = 4 × **Side**

⇒ **Perimeter** = 4 × 8

⇒ **Perimeter** = 32 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 32 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Diagonal** of a **Square**

The **diagonal** (d) of a **square** with **side** (s) is given by d = s√2.

**Area** and **Diagonal** Relation

The **area** of a **square** can also be calculated using its **diagonal** as **Area** = d² ÷ 2.

**Properties** of a **Square**

All four **sides** are equal, all four **angles** are 90°, and the **diagonals** bisect each other at right angles.

questions.question: The area of a square is 121 square cm. What is the diagonal (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Diagonal** of a **square** = √(2 × **Area**)

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(2 × 121)

⇒ **Diagonal** = 11√2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 11√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Area** of the **square** = 121 cm²

**Formula Used:**

**Area** of a **square** = (side)²

**Diagonal** of a **square** (d) = side × √2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51c4752b884a3a5c65a6326cb1600069df8f6ff097a8f639e86c0af5d2b1488b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (side)² = 121

⇒ side = √121 = 11 cm

⇒ **Diagonal** = 11 × √2

⇒ **Diagonal** = 11√2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 11√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Area and Diagonal

The **Area** of a **square** can also be expressed directly in terms of its **diagonal** (d) as: **Area** = d² ÷ 2.

Perimeter of a Square

The **Perimeter** of a **square** is the sum of all its four equal sides: **Perimeter** = 4 × side.

Properties of Square Diagonals

The **diagonals** of a **square** are equal in length, bisect each other at 90°, and bisect the vertex angles into two 45° angles.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Average** of an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** is (First term + Last term) ÷ 2 = (28 + 108) ÷ 2 = 68.

Number of terms (n) = [(Last term − First term) ÷ Common Difference] + 1 = [(108 − 28) ÷ 2] + 1 = 41.

**Sum** = Average × Number of terms = 68 × 41 = 2788.

**∴ The correct answer is 2788.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term (a) = 28

Last term (l) = 108

Common difference (d) = 30 − 28 = 2

**Formula Used:**

Number of terms (n) = [(l − a) ÷ d] + 1

Sum of n terms (Sₙ) = (n ÷ 2) × (a + l)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a9b413010e711bbd97ed38ed0faa7ef4092c88b86b898a9dc1745d547ff6be44.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ n = [(108 − 28) ÷ 2] + 1

⇒ n = (80 ÷ 2) + 1 = 40 + 1 = 41

⇒ S₄₁ = (41 ÷ 2) × (28 + 108)

⇒ S₄₁ = 20.5 × 136

⇒ S₄₁ = 2788

**∴ The correct answer is 2788.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

General Term of an AP

The n-th term of an **Arithmetic Progression** is given by Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d, where a is the first term and d is the common difference.

Alternative Sum Formula

The sum can also be calculated as Sₙ = (n/2) × [2a + (n − 1)d].

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the first n natural numbers is Σn = n(n + 1) ÷ 2.

questions.question: The average of 24 numbers is 54. A number 'M' is subtracted from each number. New average of these 24 numbers is 42. What is the value of 'M'?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a **constant value** is subtracted from every observation in a set, the **original average** also decreases by the **same value**.

New Average = Original Average − Value Subtracted (M)

42 = 54 − M

M = 54 − 42 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers in the set = **24**

Original Average = **54**

New Average after subtracting **M** from each = **42**

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of observations) ÷ (Number of observations)

Property: If xᵢ → xᵢ − M, then Averageₙₑw = Averageₒₗd − M

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76dee8b5863ff4f1e613dc560a8456f4fcebf70d39ed3da08f3137810f84f772.png] 

⇒ Original Total Sum = 24 × 54 = 1296

⇒ New Total Sum = 24 × 42 = 1008

⇒ Total decrease in sum = 1296 − 1008 = 288

⇒ Since **M** was subtracted from each of the **24 numbers**, the total decrease = 24 × M

⇒ 24 × M = 288

⇒ M = 288 ÷ 24

⇒ M = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Addition Property

If a constant **k** is added to every number in a data set, the new average is **Original Average + k**.

Multiplication Property

If every number in a data set is multiplied by **k**, the new average is **Original Average × k**.

Division Property

If every number in a data set is divided by a non-zero constant **k**, the new average is **Original Average ÷ k**.

questions.question: Average marks obtained by 20 boys is 44 (Each boy has obtained distinct value of marks). If the highest marks and lowest marks obtained are removed, then the average reduces by 4. What is the average of the highest and lowest marks obtained?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Average of removed items** = Original Average + (Total Decrease in remaining sum ÷ Number of removed items)

Total decrease in sum of 18 boys = 18 × 4 = 72

Average of Highest and Lowest = 44 + (72 ÷ 2)

Average = 44 + 36 = 80

**∴ The correct answer is 80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of **boys** (n₁) = 20

Initial **average marks** (A₁) = 44

New number of **boys** (n₂) = 18 (after removing Highest and Lowest marks)

New **average marks** (A₂) = 44 − 4 = 40

**Formula:**

Total Marks = Average × Number of students

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1062b2f71905c678895a027e04291d4ba8c24c724fc7e9c6aa3c0fb49254051c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total marks of 20 boys = 20 × 44 = 880

⇒ Total marks of 18 boys = 18 × 40 = 720

⇒ Sum of **Highest (H)** and **Lowest (L)** marks = 880 − 720 = 160

⇒ Average of Highest and Lowest marks = 160 ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 80

**∴ The correct answer is 80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exclusion Concept in Averages

When items are removed and the average decreases, the sum of removed items is greater than the original average share. Sum of excluded items = (Number of excluded items × Old Average) + (New Count × Decrease in Average).

Average of Group

The arithmetic mean or average is defined as the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Average = (x₁ + x₂ + ... + xₙ) ÷ n.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question: How many factors of the number 84 are odd numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **prime factorization** of 84 is 2² × 3¹ × 7¹.

To find the **number of odd factors**, ignore the prime base 2 and its power.

Apply the formula (a + 1)(b + 1)... to the exponents of the **odd prime factors** 3 and 7.

Number of odd factors = (1 + 1) × (1 + 1) = 2 × 2 = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number = 84

**Method:** Listing all possible factors and selecting odd numbers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d089b895f7cc95fde7e36bbdb71b6c79faa83025842ca40f2cff34e32fe38e80.png] 

⇒ List all factors of 84: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 12, 14, 21, 28, 42, 84

⇒ Filter only the **odd numbers**: 1, 3, 7, 21

⇒ Count the filtered numbers = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Number of Factors

For any number N = p₁a × p₂b × p₃c, the total number of factors is given by (a + 1)(b + 1)(c + 1).

Number of Even Factors

If N = 2a × p₁b × p₂c, the number of even factors is a × (b + 1)(c + 1), or simply Total Factors − Odd Factors.

Sum of Factors

The sum of all factors is calculated as [(p₁a⁺¹ − 1)/(p₁ − 1)] × [(p₂b⁺¹ − 1)/(p₂ − 1)] × ...

questions.question: Which is the largest number that divides 91, 127, 199 and 235 to leave the same remainder in each case?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **largest number** that leaves the **same remainder**, calculate the **differences** between the numbers.

Differences are: (127 − 91) = 36; (199 − 127) = 72; (235 − 199) = 36.

The required number is the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** of 36, 72, and 36.

HCF(36, 72, 36) = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers: 91, 127, 199, and 235.

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = **HCF** of (|N₂ − N₁|, |N₃ − N₂|, |N₄ − N₃|)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20b3fe6c8a7d5fc0e4ffab81781388d2c3ff88a11ef117b33a157fc2ba375fca.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ First difference = 127 − 91 = 36

⇒ Second difference = 199 − 127 = 72

⇒ Third difference = 235 − 199 = 36

⇒ Prime factorization of 36 = 2² × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 72 = 2³ × 3²

⇒ **HCF** = 2² × 3² = 4 × 9 = 36

⇒ Verify: 91 ÷ 36 = 2 (rem. 19), 127 ÷ 36 = 3 (rem. 19), 199 ÷ 36 = 5 (rem. 19), 235 ÷ 36 = 6 (rem. 19).

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

It is the **greatest divisor** that exactly divides two or more numbers. For "same remainder" problems, always find the **HCF of the differences** between numbers.

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest number which is **exactly divisible** by each of the given numbers. Relationship: Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM.

Divisibility Rule of 36

A number is divisible by 36 if it is simultaneously divisible by both **4** (last two digits) and **9** (sum of digits).

questions.question: Cost price of an article is Rs. 450. The profit percentage is 20 percent. What is the value of profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Profit** is calculated as a percentage of the **Cost Price (CP)**.

**20%** is equivalent to the fraction **1/5**.

Profit = 1/5 × 450 = 90.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** = Rs. 450

**Profit Percentage** = 20%

**Formula Used:**

**Profit = (Profit % × Cost Price) ÷ 100**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f6ad2e250dd875ac6126eb2d8b76a26bd7624748c9b7c6a7a651efff80ea6a5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit = (20 × 450) ÷ 100

⇒ Profit = 9000 ÷ 100

⇒ Profit = 90

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Selling Price (SP)

The price at which an article is sold is called the Selling Price. **SP = CP + Profit** or **SP = CP − Loss**.

Profit Percentage

Profit % is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise. Formula: **Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100**.

Marked Price (MP)

The price printed or labeled on an article. Discounts are always calculated on the **Marked Price**.

The difference between **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)** is the **Profit** or **Loss**.

Given **Profit percentage** = 40% and **Profit amount** = Rs. 100.

40% units → Rs. 100

1% unit → 100 ÷ 40 = Rs. 2.5

**Selling Price** = CP (100%) + Profit (40%) = 140%

140% → 140 × 2.5 = 350

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 40/25 of the first number. The second number is what percent of the first number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Sum** to **First Number** = 40 : 25.

**Second Number** = 40 − 25 = 15 units.

Required percentage = (Second Number ÷ First Number) × 100.

⇒ (15 ÷ 25) × 100 = 60%.

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of two numbers = 40/25 × First Number.

**Formula Used:** Percentage = (Value ÷ Base Value) × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d7f06e5cecc1bf3e22bd3f8118647dda99ef775e0c2e962d6cf020f74ed04b0c.png] 

⇒ Let the **First Number** be x and the **Second Number** be y.

⇒ x + y = (40/25) × x

⇒ y = (40/25)x − x

⇒ y = (40x − 25x) ÷ 25

⇒ y = 15x ÷ 25

⇒ y/x = 15/25 = 3/5

⇒ Percentage = (y/x) × 100 = (3/5) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

To convert any fraction a/b into a percentage, multiply the fraction by 100 and add the % symbol.

Percentage Base Identification

In the phrase 'A is what percent of B', B is always the base (denominator) and A is the numerator.

Ratio and Sum Property

If the ratio of Sum : First Number is m : n, then the ratio of Second Number : First Number is (m − n) : n.

questions.question: A car covers two distances of 44 km and 76 km in total 30 hours. Car covered both the distances at the same speed. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the car?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the **Speed** is the same for both segments, we can use the **Total Distance** divided by **Total Time**.

**Total Distance** = 44 km + 76 km = 120 km

**Total Time** = 30 hr

**Speed** = 120 ÷ 30 = 4 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 4 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Distance₁** = 44 km

**Distance₂** = 76 km

**Total Time** = 30 hr

**Speed** = constant (v)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d9ca687ce4ae4cd009105c107cbf47abed841479dabc8a0a7134999813077a68.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Speed** = **Distance** ÷ **Time**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the constant speed be v km/hr.

⇒ Time taken for first distance = 44 ÷ v

⇒ Time taken for second distance = 76 ÷ v

⇒ Total Time = (44 ÷ v) + (76 ÷ v) = 30

⇒ (44 + 76) ÷ v = 30

⇒ 120 ÷ v = 30

⇒ v = 120 ÷ 30

⇒ v = 4 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 4 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Formula

When a body travels different distances with different speeds, **Average Speed** = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**.

Speed-Distance Proportionality

When **Time** is constant, **Distance** is directly proportional to **Speed** (D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: If (4x + 3y) : (4x - 3y) = 14 : 5, then what is the value of x : y?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Componendo and Dividendo** rule: If (a + b) / (a − b) = p / q, then a / b = (p + q) / (p − q).

Given (4x + 3y) / (4x − 3y) = 14 / 5.

Let a = 4x and b = 3y, then 4x / 3y = (14 + 5) / (14 − 5) = 19 / 9.

Now, x / y = (19 / 9) × (3 / 4) = 19 / 12.

Multiply both terms of the ratio 19 : 12 by 3 to match the options → 57 : 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 57 : 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The ratio (4x + 3y) : (4x − 3y) = 14 : 5.

**Formula Used:** We use the **Cross-multiplication** method for solving linear equations in two variables involving **Ratios**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1afcb5a17e148e7b3e00cf427236f57eecaacc5213a1abf03c86fcf9d28c949a.png] 

⇒ (4x + 3y) / (4x − 3y) = 14 / 5

⇒ 5 × (4x + 3y) = 14 × (4x − 3y)

⇒ 20x + 15y = 56x − 42y

⇒ 15y + 42y = 56x − 20x

⇒ 57y = 36x

⇒ x / y = 57 / 36

⇒ x : y = 57 : 36

**∴ The correct answer is 57 : 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Componendo and Dividendo

A theorem used to solve equations involving ratios. If a/b = c/d, then (a+b)/(a−b) = (c+d)/(c−d).

Duplicate and Triplicate Ratios

The duplicate ratio of a : b is a² : b², and the triplicate ratio is a³ : b³.

Alternendo and Invertendo

If a : b = c : d, then by Alternendo a : c = b : d, and by Invertendo b : a = d : c.

questions.question: The expenditure and savings of a person are in ratio of 7 : 2 respectively. His savings increase by 1/3 of his income and income remains the same. What is the new respective ratio of his expenditure and savings?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio of **Expenditure** : **Savings** = 7 : 2 ⇒ **Income** = 7 + 2 = 9 units.

Increase in **Savings** = 1/3 × **Income** = 1/3 × 9 = 3 units.

Since **Income** is constant, this increase comes directly from **Expenditure**.

New **Savings** = 2 + 3 = 5 units | New **Expenditure** = 7 − 3 = 4 units.

New Ratio = 4 : 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of **Expenditure** to **Savings** = 7 : 2.

**Formula Used:** **Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab3a4358f8f6b987d30274f7acd4ebda41686474a541871131c21fd2bd941076.png] 

Let **Expenditure** = 7x and **Savings** = 2x.

⇒ **Income** = 7x + 2x = 9x.

⇒ Increase in **Savings** = 1/3 × 9x = 3x.

⇒ New **Savings** = 2x + 3x = 5x.

⇒ New **Expenditure** = **Total Income** − New **Savings**

⇒ New **Expenditure** = 9x − 5x = 4x.

⇒ New Ratio = 4x : 5x = 4 : 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Concept

The fundamental relation is **Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**. Any change in one component must be balanced by others if the total income is fixed.

Ratio Balancing

When a fraction of one quantity is moved to another while the total remains constant, the sum of the ratio parts does not change.

Percentage Change in Income

If **Income** increases by x%, **Expenditure** by y%, and **Savings** by z%, then: (Initial E × y%) + (Initial S × z%) = (Initial I × x%).
